honesty: THE PRIZE PROBLEM IS NOT CLOSED. `erdos_20` asks whether f(n,k) < c_k^n. Nothing here bears on the upper-bound side beyond the 1960 Erdos-Rado n! bound. The modern record (Alweiss-Lovett-Wu-Zhang 2019, sharpened by Rao and by Bell-Chueluecha-Warnke) is f(n,k) <= (O(k log n))^n; it is NOT formalized here and was not attempted.

lower_k3 (base sqrt 6 ~ 2.449 at k=3) beats the Erdos-Rado product construction (base 2) and beats the estate's own formalized baseline. It is NOT a literature record: better k=3 lower-bound constructions are known (Abbott-Hanson-Sauer 1972 and successors, base around 3.16). The claim banked is exactly `6^t < f (2t) 3`, no more.
f_one and f_two are exact values of f, but they are small/easy cases; f(n,k) is not known exactly for any n >= 2, k >= 3.
erdos_rado_bound is the classical 1960 theorem. The contribution is that it is now MACHINE-CHECKED and that Mathlib had no sunflower lemma at all - not that the mathematics is new.
open: erdos_20 : answer(sorry) <-> exists c, forall n k, n>0 -> f n k < (c k)^n  -- THE $1000 QUESTION, untouched.

The ALWZ/Rao (O(k log n))^n upper bound - the real modern frontier - is unformalized. This is the single highest-value next Lean target on this problem and is a genuine multi-week formalization (it needs the spread-approximation / sunflower-free encoding machinery).

Exact f(2,3): f_two_three banks 6 < f(2,3) <= 9. The true value is 7; the matching upper bound f(2,3) <= 7 (a 3-sunflower-free 2-uniform family has max degree <= 2 and no 3-matching, hence <= 6 edges) is NOT formalized. Cheap next win.

A better seed for the multiplier: any explicit k-sunflower-free n-uniform family of size M > 6^(n/2) at k=3 plugs straight into hasWitness_of_finset + HasWitness.mul and raises the base with zero further proof work. This is the cheapest path to matching the literature lower bound.
Kostochka-type improvements of the n! factor in the upper bound: unformalized.
